# worklog — project_waitlist_reservations (env_0082), M=2

## Step 0 — pre-check and draws
- Read: references (product_extended.yaml, task_tools.py, task.json), blueprint.yaml, products/waitlist.yaml, home/garden/access plan parameters and the home charge, true-up, transfer, cancellation, credit-correction and billing rules, db_schema, share_tools (verification K=2), coordinator files XF_recipe.md, realism_bar.md, owner_ruling.md.
- Draws: task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [5, 4]; task 1 -> prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6, 5, 6, 4].
- DECISION (DSL limit, no explicit route): the frozen compute DSL reads only the reservation, its offers/notices and the customer's holdings/ledgers in other categories; projects and utility_accounts are unreadable. Closest established rule (XF C5: "scope the policy by a coarse exact record test via a self-naming overwrite; out of scope = the base rule restated verbatim"): every extended computation is scoped to reservations whose household already holds a share on the offered project (or a closed share being restored); those records carry the array's output, credit value and design output. Offers outside that scope stay under the base rule verbatim.
- DECISION: status-only events (decline, expiry, lapse, reinstatement, reconfirmation, withdrawal) carry no number a factor can bear on and are not claimed as problems; each task's owner=user problem is the customer's own request change (owner_ruling (a): the subscriber submits the change).

## REWORK round 2 — LEVER CATALOGUE (AMENDMENT 1.2)
Scope of every computation: a Residential-line reservation (Relocation Priority, Residential Standard, Residential Add-On) whose customer holds Residential (home) shares; utility_accounts and projects are outside DSL reach (AMENDMENT 1.5).
- Waitlist P keys. USED: increment_kw (restore/fit sizing step), estimate_years (estimate), min_requested_kw (restore scope), offer_response_days (respond_by_date, tool body). UNUSABLE: priority_rank, eligible_customer_types, eligible_target_lines, eligible_programs, requires_open_subscription, requires_income_eligibility, requires_relocation_event, relocation_window_days, requires_partner_referral (eligibility switches, constant within each class, amount-neutral); max_requested_kw (bound only, never reached); sizing_cap_pct, min_annual_usage_kwh, usage_data_max_age_months, utility_data_authorization_required (read only against utility_accounts, outside DSL); max_open_reservations_in_class, any_project_in_territory, capacity_set_aside_pct (queue mechanics, amount-neutral); max_declines_before_lapse, expired_offer_counts_as_decline, queue_date_reset_on_decline, decline_partial_without_penalty, reconfirm_*, reinstatement_days, kw_increase_resets_queue_date, kw_decrease_allowed, utility_account_change_allowed, queue_date_kept_on_move, removal_on_final_bill, lapse_on_conversion_elsewhere, waive_reconfirm_when_offer_pending, one_open_offer_per_reservation, confirmation_days, queue_date_basis, offer_order_tiebreak, position_notice_interval_months (lifecycle switches and dates, amount-neutral for kW and estimates); partial_offer_allowed, min_partial_offer_pct, min_offer_kw (validity tests of an offer, base content kept); default_conversion_plan, conversion_rate_lock_days (plan choice / lock, amount-neutral); business_credit_review_before_offer, income_verification_before_offer (false in the three classes); estimate_rounding (base rounding, kept).
- waitlist_reservations fields. USED: requested_kw, requested_plan, project_id, utility_account_id, variant_name (scope), status (gate), queue_date (gate order). UNUSABLE: target_line, conversion_kind (constant per class), partner_code (empty in these classes), submitted_date, reconfirm_due_date, declines_counted, closed_date, closure_reason (lifecycle only, no amount rule in the charter turns on them).
- waitlist_offers fields. USED: offer_date, offered_kw, estimated_annual_kwh, project_id (fit target-yield source, reservation-scoped). UNUSABLE: offered_plan (equals requested_plan in scope), estimated_annual_savings (an estimate, never a rate source; reading it would re-use a recorded amount, X3), respond_by_date (lifecycle).
- waitlist_notices fields. UNUSABLE for amounts: notice_date, respond_by_date, queue_position (no charter amount rule turns on them); seeded as own-category history where the base schedule produces them (O6).
- Home holdings (CFIELD). USED: home_sub_id, status, project_id, utility_account_id, allocation_kw, closed_date, closure_reason. UNUSABLE: contract_kw (never rewritten by filings, X3 vs allocation_kw), billing_type (consolidated vs dual changes no credited kWh or credit value; benefit_basis forbids pricing by it), sales_channel, signed_date, approved_date (no estimate or sizing rule turns on them), activation_date (share start is not array age: AMENDMENT 1.5 proxy ban, F2), term_end_date, notice_date, scheduled_end_date, move_out_date, pending_utility_account_id, removal_notice_date (lifecycle).
- Home plan params (CPARAM). USED: production_guarantee_pct (design-yield recovery from a guarantee row), savings_rate_pct (base estimate). UNUSABLE: sizing_cap_pct, oversize_review_threshold_pct, resize_target_pct (constant across the reachable plans, or read only against utility usage outside DSL), every billing / fee / ETF / deposit / rescission / transfer key (charges, not estimates or sizes; benefit_basis), annual_review_enabled (switch, true on the reachable plans), term_months (no estimate rule turns on term).
- home_credits. USED: credited_kwh, credit_value, banked_value, posted_date, event_type (posted / reversed). UNUSABLE: statement_month (the DSL windows on posted_date; a second window field would be a duplicate reading), utility_account_id (equals the share's own).
- home_reviews. USED: contract_year, review_date, credited_kwh_12m, usage_kwh_12m, guaranteed_kwh, shortfall_kwh, avg_credit_rate, resize_kw. UNUSABLE: guarantee_credit (a recorded amount, X3 against shortfall_kwh × rate already used), period_start_month / period_end_month (fixed by review_date), outcome (names the result of fields already read).
- home_allocations. USED: kw, effective_date, filing_reason, event_type. UNUSABLE: filing_month (same date dimension as effective_date), home_request_id (link only).
- home_billing / home_requests. UNUSABLE: every amount is a charge, payment, fee or credit (benefit_basis; no estimate or sizing rule turns on payment history); requests are read for closure only.
- Other categories (biz, access, garden, farm, civic). UNUSABLE: the worlds' customers hold none, and the residential estimate and sizing rules turn on no other line's figures except through account sizing, which reads utility usage (outside DSL).
- R6 inventory after this catalogue: banked_value_allowance and banking_margin (company practice on recorded banked_value), young_share_blend (credibility weights on the recorded line count and assessed guarantee), credit_rate_trend (company estimating schedule on recorded true-up rates) and the single-shortfall midpoint tier of the two guarantee floors; each taken because the catalogue above leaves no unused honest R1-R5 lever on that computation in that world.
